inuit.d: a member of a people inhabiting the Arctic (northern Canada or Greenland or Alaska or eastern Siberia)
e: the Algonquians called them Eskimo (“eaters of raw flesh”) but they call themselves the Inuit (“the people”)

inundation.d: the rising of a body of water and its overflowing onto normally dry land

inunction.d: anointing as part of a religious ceremony or healing ritual

inutility.d: the quality of having no practical use

inulin.d: used to manufacture fructose and in assessing kidney function

inure.d: cause to accept or become hardened to; habituate

inundate.d: fill quickly beyond capacity; as with a liquid

inunct.d: administer an oil or ointment to; often in a religious ceremony of blessing
